An unlawful homicide committed by a Minister of country X abroad is generally classified as an act jure imperii if done in an official capacity, but as a private act (jure gestionis) if purely personal and unrelated to official functions. However, under international law, a foreign court may hear any case against a minister regardless of the nature of the act, as such conduct is treated as personal for jurisdictional purposes.
